newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was quiet, with no reported sales as packers and owners remained in a standoff, feedlot sources said.
Reports of some packers raising bids $1.00 to last week's top of $64.00 failed to nudge owners away from asking levels of $65.00 or $66.00, they said. Most bids were at $63.00.
Cattle owners were holding out for higher prices amid ideas that strong beef demand would stimulate strong packer buying, sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.03 to $1.02 per cwt on 175 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said.
Brisk sales last week and the ability for feedlots to remain extremely current in their marketings also fueled higher price outlooks for fed cattle this week, several cattle feeders said.
Showlists this week were estimated unchanged to smaller than last week, with parts of this week's showlists reportedly sold late last week, they said.

Friday's USDA Cattle on Feed report, which showed greater- than-expected January placements at 125 percent of a year ago, failed to weigh on cash cattle prices as the industry focused on tight near-term supplies, a Kansas source noted.
